title: Credit Suisse celebrates Pride. Putting a spotlight on LGBT inclusion.
description: As many Credit Suisse employees around the world join in Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender (LGBT) Pride celebrations over the coming weeks, Antoinette Poschung, Global Head of Human Resources, spoke with Adrian Köstli, Staff, IWM and LGBT & Ally Network committee member.  The two talked about the importance of employees feeling comfortable to bring their whole identity to work. They also discussed the role of LGBT allies and how we are creating an ever more diverse and inclusive workplace at Credit Suisse.

asr.full_text: Good morning Adrien. Nice to meet you. It's always a great pleasure to meet an employee, you know from a younger generation. Thank you for the opportunity to speak about the topic of LGBT inclusiveness. It's a pleasure to speak with you about a topic that's very dear to my heart and where I'm very engaged in the LGBTI and Ally network.. We have now a particular month right? It's June and July and we have an anniversary. Yes, we are celebrating LGBT Pride and it's around the globe. Here in Europe it's in June where we think back of 50 years of the Stonewall riots in New York. In addition to that we have 25 years of Zurich Pride. in New York. In addition to that, we have twenty five years of Zurich Pride. This is why we celebrate. It's great to see that Credit Suisse is even more visible this year and also, it's great to see our senior leaders speaking up for that topic. The overall message we want to give employees is that we really embrace diversity. You know, that we are an inclusive employer. What does this mean for you Adrian? For me, it's very important that I can be myself at work. Because if I have to hide a part of my life, it takes a lot of energy and this energy can be used far better, for example in creating your successful career. For me it has also something to do with dignity and respect from for human beings and you know Being an employee you bring your whole identity to work as well. Absolutely, and Antoinette I saw you also signed up as an LGBT Ally. That was really cool that you sent me an email and encouraged me to sign up for an Ally. Why is this Ally concept so important? Well, it is important that we show other employees that it's okay to be different. And I think every employee can play a role in shaping the norms and the culture at Credit Suisse. As an LGBT ally the simplest thing you can do is really stand up for lgbt equality and inclusiveness for example by showing it with our LGBT mousepad or even by addressing negative behaviour you can stand up, speak up against misbehavior. So that you know if you stand up that you have an ally in the room. It can be really simple by just showing that it is okay but it can also be taking an action in terms of if there was a joke that was not appropriate to stand up. Yeah, I think it think also in terms of, I mean, if you look at the our clients, they're also very diverse, right? And, therefore, I think it's absolutely understood and saying which is really natural that the workforce is also very diverse. Absolutely. As we expect accept our clients to be different, we also accept our employees to be different. so the balance on credit is diverse and our workforce is also very diverse. Yes, absolutely. As we expect accept our clients to be different we also should accept our employees to be different. And even if there are some clients who would not like it we would stand up for our values because I think this is really a very very strong value for Credit Suisse which I'm also very proud of. And we probably would want to thank all of our employees who help each day to make Credit Suisse really so inclusive. CHIASY VANSHOOKENFELDTENGENEVEKELNENSEE Thank you to the 3,800 allies we have globally and to all employees who support us. And we wish all the employees a really happy celebration. Happy Pride. Happy Pride, exactly.

The interview format and closing Credit Suisse logo reflect ordinary corporate communication, with no financial offer, payment request, credential request, or required participation shown.
